solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Act strangely by a fellow doctor’s burial place

indicators.note: doing something strangely means doing it in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
co- is the prefix for a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone behaves oddly beside a colleague's grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like a verb doing the acting, but it is the raw material for 'strangely'. The 's after doctor reads as 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs, as under ancient Rome.

clue.text: Work for church area, getting round a formal curse

indicators.note: to get round something is to go about it, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: an anthem is a choral piece sung in church services
A is the standard abbreviation for area
taken as written, the letter that goes inside

explanation.surface: Church music and a church area, oddly tied up with an excommunication curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work for church' looks like the definition, but the curse at the end is what is defined; the choral piece only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a solemn ecclesiastical curse of excommunication, so a formal curse is its original meaning.

clue.text: Friendly communication accompanying a note

indicators.note: one thing accompanying another goes along beside it, so the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: taken as written
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire

explanation.surface: A friendly message sent along with a short written note.
explanation.walkthrough: The telegram is named first in the clue, but accompanying means it goes alongside, here after the note. Cable for telegram is an old-fashioned usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are good-natured and peaceable, a straightforward synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Tender-sounding old king?

indicators.note: something that sounds like a word is heard as it, so we want a spelling matching that sound

blocks.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: A king whose name sounds gentle and soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' tempts as soft or loving; here it is the verb meaning to present a bid. Offa was an 8th-century king of Mercia in England, builder of Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, so he is a historical monarch from over a millennium ago.

clue.text: Composition everyone has asked about

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to ask or command
all means every person

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that everybody has been enquiring about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asked' wants the modern sense, but the setter needs the archaic past tense of bid, which surrounds the word for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballade is a piece of music or a verse form, such as Chopin's piano ballades, so it is a musical or poetic work.

clue.text: Liqueur new teacher initially refused us

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new teacher turns down the offer of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACHER + R + US rearranged. 'New' reads as describing the teacher but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks in France, in green and yellow varieties.

clue.text: Terms EMI arranged for speechless actor

indicators.note: arranging items puts them in a new order, so the letters are sorted differently

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A record company agrees a contract for a performer who does not talk.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI is a British record label, which makes the surface about a recording deal; both words are simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimester is a performer of mime, who acts out stories through gesture alone without saying a word.

clue.text: Example of trendy attitude

blocks.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stance is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: A case of someone striking a fashionable pose.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + STANCE; 'of' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or occurrence cited to illustrate something, as in 'for instance'.

clue.text: Article penned by an Edinburgh man, possibly, in Greek

indicators.note: what is penned by something is shut in by it, as animals in a pen, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the definite article
taken as written, the outer word
Ian is the Scottish form of John; 'possibly' marks it as just one example of a name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman writing an article in the Greek language.
explanation.walkthrough: A(THE)N + IAN. Ian is a typically Scottish first name, hence an Edinburgh man.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian is a native of Athens, the Greek capital, so the noun names a particular kind of Greek person.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid provided by graduates almost entirely

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the phrase falls one letter short at the end

blocks.note: BAs are holders of Bachelor of Arts degrees
'in full' means completely, entirely

explanation.surface: Graduates supply nearly all of some amount of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: BAS + IN FUL(L), with the last letter cut. 'Almost entirely' reads as a single adverb but splits into signal and source.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinful is the amount a basin holds, a measure of water or other liquid.

clue.text: See Republican president film a small parrot

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A Republican president watching a movie about a little parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: LO + R + IKE + ET. Ike, a Republican, makes the surface hang together, though R and IKE come from separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorikeets are small, brightly coloured Australasian birds of the parrot family that feed on nectar.

clue.text: Important frontier penetrated by a communicator on line

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed into it, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: key means crucial, important
a border is a frontier between countries
taken as written, the letter that goes inside

explanation.surface: A key border crossing breached by someone sending messages over the wire.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY + BO(A)RDER. 'On line' makes the solver think of a phone line, but a keyboarder types messages into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboarder is someone who types at a keyboard, so they communicate online by typing text.

clue.text: A rift so restricting a northern plant

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in or confine, so the outer words close around something

blocks.note: taken as written
a rift is a gap or break
thus means so, therefore
taken as written, inside
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A split that keeps a northern plant in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A northern plant' reads as one phrase, but only 'plant' is the definition; 'a northern' gives the two letters held in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus is a South African flowering plant, the African lily, with rounded heads of blue or white blooms.

clue.text: Stagger, having knocked time off dangerous exploit

indicators.note: knocking something off removes it, so a letter is struck out of the word

blocks.note: a stunt is a daring, risky feat
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A daredevil reels after shaving seconds off a risky feat.
explanation.walkthrough: STUNT with its T for time knocked off. 'Stagger' is the verb meaning astonish, not reel about.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or shock them deeply, which is what stunning them means too.

clue.text: Willing, mostly light music group in Indonesia

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: game means ready and willing, as in 'game for anything'
to light is to land, come down, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A keen but rather light-hearted musical ensemble in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME + LAN(D). 'Light music' reads as one idea, but 'light' is the verb meaning settle, cut by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamelan is a traditional Javanese or Balinese percussion orchestra of gongs and metallophones.

clue.text: Relative extremely generous about investing foreign cash

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outermost letters
to invest originally meant to clothe or surround, so the outer letters wrap something

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the rand is South Africa's currency
on means about, concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A very generous relative puts money in overseas currency.
explanation.walkthrough: G(RAND)S + ON. 'Investing' suggests finance, but it means surrounding here.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is the son of one's child, a family member and so a relative.

clue.text: Motion principally marking leaderless aristocracy

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so the opening letter is used
without a leader means the front is missing, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the nobility is the aristocratic class

explanation.surface: A debate motion criticising an aristocracy that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: M + (N)OBILITY. 'Motion' looks like a parliamentary proposal but is the definition, meaning movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobility is the ability to move freely, so it is closely related to movement or motion.

clue.text: Report of unsecured vessel in European lake

indicators.note: a report is something heard, a spoken account, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: loose means unsecured and an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: News of a boat drifting free on a lake in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat on the lake; it is a vase, an urn. Said aloud, the phrase matches the place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Lucerne is a large lake in central Switzerland, named after the city on its shore.

clue.text: European woman outside is Sweden’s first envoy

indicators.note: first means the leading letter of the word
to be outside something is to surround it, so one piece encloses others

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Mary is a woman's name
taken as written
the opening letter of the country

explanation.surface: A European woman becomes Sweden's first diplomat abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman's name is split open to hold the short word plus the country's initial; the European letter stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a diplomatic mission as a representative, the same role as an envoy.

clue.text: Deficiency in restaurant for VIPs?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: there are none of the places diners sit at
second meaning: important, distinguished people

explanation.surface: Even celebrities find a fully booked restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TABLES the answer describes a restaurant with nowhere to sit; read whole it means important people.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are prominent, distinguished persons, the same group as very important people or dignitaries.

clue.text: Clothing a reindeer herder going north carries about

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means travelling upward, so the word reads from bottom to top
to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Lapps, or Sami, herd reindeer in northern Scandinavia
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A reindeer herder heading north carries spare garments.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'going north' means read upward. The Lapps, now usually called Sami, are the reindeer-herding people of Arctic Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments, so it means the same as clothing or attire.

clue.text: French priest born in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means inside, so one letter is placed within a name

blocks.note: Abe is the first name of Abraham Lincoln
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A French cleric who was born in the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: AB(B)E. Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is US president Abe Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title for a priest or cleric, so it describes a Catholic churchman in France.

clue.text: Acknowledge download I devoured about park

indicators.note: about means around, so the earlier words wrap round something

blocks.note: an app is a program you download
taken as written
devoured means ate greedily
a rec is a recreation ground, a public park

explanation.surface: Admitting that I gobbled up a download about a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the preceding words round the park, which lands just after the download. A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something can mean to recognise or be grateful for it, as when acknowledging help.

clue.text: Data distributed with mail in an Adriatic region

indicators.note: distributed things are spread about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Information sent out by post across a region by the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a postal service; the two words just provide letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is the coastal region of Croatia along the eastern Adriatic Sea, home of the spotted dog breed.

clue.text: Raised objections, seeing fag end

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down clue a word lifted upward reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone complained on spotting a cigarette butt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised objections' reads as complained, but 'Raised' is the signal and objections are buts. A fag end is British slang for a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short remaining piece of something used up, such as a cigarette or a pencil.

clue.text: Italian union leader admitted to gathering in formal way

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the opening letter is used
something admitted to a place is let inside it

blocks.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian
the opening letter of the word
a rally is a mass gathering or meeting

explanation.surface: An Italian trade union boss is let into a meeting with due ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: R(IT + U)ALLY. 'Union leader' reads as a trade unionist but yields just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Done ritually means performed according to set ceremony or custom, that is, in a formal manner.

clue.text: It may be shed? Not in onset of heat by river

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word counts

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
the opening letter of the word
the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York

explanation.surface: Something that can be cast off, as long as you are not in the warmth near water.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT + H + OUSE. 'Shed' tempts as the verb to cast off, but it is the noun, a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small building separate from a main house, and a shed is one example of it.

clue.text: East Ender’s pastime adopted by lean government influencer

indicators.note: Londoners from the East End traditionally drop their aitches, so the word loses its initial h
something adopted is taken in, so this piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a hobby is a leisure pastime
to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A Londoner's hobby taken up by a thin political operator.
explanation.walkthrough: L('OBBY)IST. The Cockney of London's East End drops the h, giving 'obby. 'Lean' looks like thin but is the verb, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobbyist is paid to persuade legislators to support particular causes, so they try to sway government policy.
